shadows.name: sheet
shadows.value: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--carve-drop) 70%, transparent), 0 2px 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--carve-drop) 50%, transparent), 0 20px 44px -20px var(--carve-popover-far)
shadows.purpose: The stage, and nothing else — the window's one resting elevation (POD-725).

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: The transient tier: menus, pickers, drag ghosts, the save bar.

shadows.name: inset-carve
shadows.value: inset 0 3px 7px -2px var(--carve-engraved), inset 0 -1px 0 color-mix(in oklab, var(--border) 45%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: A field pressed INTO its surface — the operator's prompt, the standby panel. All that survives of the engraved idiom.

shadows.name: engraved
shadows.value: inset 3px 0 6px -3px var(--carve-engraved), inset -3px 0 6px -3px var(--carve-engraved), inset 0 3px 6px -3px var(--carve-engraved)
shadows.purpose: RETIRED (POD-725): the recessed middle column became the gutter-and-sheet. Token still defined, paints nothing.

shadows.name: engraved-bar
shadows.purpose: RETIRED (POD-725): the folded bar keeps the deck's own gradient and inset instead.

shadows.name: bar-drop
shadows.purpose: RETIRED: no compact section bar casts a fold shadow any more.

motion.name: phase-crossfade
motion.purpose: Issue-color crossfade via registered --issue @property; gated on prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: phase-morph
motion.purpose: One-shot agent phase changes, followed by total stillness.

motion.name: working-mark
motion.purpose: The only canonical working mark, shown only while an agent computes or a sent message is in transport; it rests fully lit under reduced motion.

motion.name: working-meter
motion.purpose: A worklist row's running segment sweeps only while a session on that row is computing.

motion.name: structural-layout
motion.purpose: One-shot layout transitions for rows, branches, seats, and stage changes; latched against first paint and gated on prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Superade Yellow signal action; dark ink, presses down 1px.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #f5c518; color: #16171a; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 6px; font: 500 14px/1 'Geist Variable', sans-serif; transition: background 150ms, transform 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: rgba(245,197,24,0.8); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: #f5c518; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(245,197,24,0.5); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Neutral action chip on the dark-ink chassis.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: #252830; color: #d7dae0; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid #3a3f48; border-radius: 6px; font: 500 14px/1 'Geist Variable', sans-serif; transition: background 150ms; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #2c3038; color: #f2f3f5; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(245,197,24,0.35); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Chrome-level quiet action; gains only a muted wash.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #a8adb6; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 6px; font: 500 14px/1 'Geist Variable', sans-serif; transition: background 150ms, color 150ms; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #252830; color: #f2f3f5; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(245,197,24,0.35); }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Red tint, never a solid red slab.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: rgba(229,48,63,0.15); color: #e5303f; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 6px; font: 500 14px/1 'Geist Variable', sans-serif; transition: background 150ms; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: rgba(229,48,63,0.28); } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: rgba(229,48,63,0.4); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(229,48,63,0.25); }

components.name: Input
components.description: Compact field on the app background; ring focus, no glow.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: #16171a; color: #d7dae0; padding: 8px 10px; border: 1px solid #3a3f48; border-radius: 4.8px; font: 400 14px/1.4 'Geist Variable', sans-serif; transition: box-shadow 150ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #6f7580; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(245,197,24,0.4); }

components.name: Mono Section Label
components.css: .ds-label-mono { font-family: 'Geist Mono Variable', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 8.5px; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #949aa4; }

components.name: Quota Chip
components.description: Header chip: dim mono-adjacent text plus a 34x3.5px meter.
components.css: .ds-quota-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; color: #6f7580; font: 400 10.5px/1 'Geist Variable', sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-meter { display: inline-block; width: 34px; height: 3.5px; border-radius: 2px; background: #3a3f48; overflow: hidden; } .ds-meter-fill { display: block; width: 60%; height: 100%; background: #6f9dff; }

narrative.overview: A stage where the work performs and the operator conducts. Dozens of agents run at once; the interface is the podium the conductor stands on — everything visible at a glance, nothing shouting for attention it hasn't earned. Superade Yellow is the winner's color: it marks the primary action and the one thing that needs you now, against a neutral dark-ink chassis. Fast, calm, precise, technical — Linear-grade density and instant interactions, with terminal honesty at its core.
keyCharacteristics: Compact 12px-base type scale; density is a feature, not a compromise
One brand yellow used as signal, never as decoration
Surfaces separated by tonal tier and hairline seam; the window spends exactly one resting elevation, and it is spent on the stage
Issue colors as translucent tints over surfaces, never flat fills
Stillness means 'needs you' — the only perpetual motion is an agent actually working

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Yellow marks the primary action or the thing waiting on you — one voice per screen region. If yellow appears somewhere nothing is asked of the operator, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Tint, Never Fill Rule
rules.body: Issue colors color-mix into their base surface at prescribed percentages. A flat fill of an issue color is prohibited.

rules.name: The Reserved Hues Rule
rules.body: Terracotta (Claude), the motion colors, and the theme's signal hues are excluded from the issue palette so state and identity never collide.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Anything the system says about itself — labels, timers, counts, IDs, terminal — is Geist Mono. Anything addressed to the human is Geist Sans.

rules.name: The Carved Rule (amended, POD-725)
rules.body: If a resting surface needs to look different from its neighbor, change its tone or draw a hairline; it may not lift. The stage sheet is the single exception, and it is not a licence — the sheet reads as elevated because it is the only thing that does. Drop shadows are otherwise for things that will disappear.

rules.name: The Frame Lifts (POD-725, POD-737)
rules.body: Both themes step UP from their ground rather than cutting the chrome into it, and the stage ends up the brightest surface in each. Dark Ink: ground #16171a → work list and dock #191a1e → bar #1b1d21 → rail #1e2024 → tab strip #202228 → sheet #23262d → chip #252830. Paper: rail #eceae4 → ground #f2f1ed → work list #f4f3f0 → bar #f7f7f5 → tab strip #faf9f7 → sheet #ffffff. The old navy ramp ran the other way, with the bar as the darkest tier.

rules.name: Carving in light (Paper, POD-725)
rules.body: The carve ink is the theme's, never black: Paper carves in #1d1c19 at 7% (engraved) and 10% (drop), because tone already groups the chrome in ~1 L-point steps. Only the two genuinely floating inks go deep — --carve-popover-far at 30%, for the popover and the stage sheet.

rules.name: The color belongs to the mission (POD-697)
rules.body: A color slot is set on top-level tasks only. Everything downstream inherits that mission color, so a sub-task offers no color picker of its own.

rules.name: The predicate, not the device (POD-516 R3)
rules.body: Perpetual motion is licensed only by an agent computing right now. Any surface-specific motion must gate on the same predicate and depict the thing that predicate is about.

rules.name: One mark, every surface (POD-1252)
rules.body: Use the eight-dot braille cell with a 1.5s travelling wave as the only working mark. It scales by context, always uses the reserved working blue, and renders only while a session computes or a sent message is in transport. Under reduced motion, the wave stops and the cell rests fully lit.

rules.name: Structural motion is not state motion
rules.body: Layout changes use a latched 200–260ms one-shot transition and never replay on first paint. They do not spend the stillness budget and must honor prefers-reduced-motion.

dos: Do use Superade Yellow only where action or attention is being asked — The Signal Rule.
Do tint issue-colored surfaces with color-mix over their base at the prescribed percentages; pair every colored surface with its quieter Flow Grey fallback.
Do keep controls on the compact scale: 32px buttons, 12px type, 4px spacing grid, 6-10px radii.
Do put machine voice (labels, timers, IDs, counts) in Geist Mono with tabular-nums where digits tick.
Do separate surfaces by tonal tier and hairline seam, and carve inward when a field must read as pressed in; reserve drop shadows for the stage and for what will disappear.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: the issue-color crossfade and phase morphs already gate on it; new motion must too.

Do cap the transcript's measure on the COLUMN, not on anything inside it (POD-993, amending POD-747). POD-747 removed two nested caps and was right about the defect: caps on the row and on the prose produced three different right edges inside one pane, with the composer and the tail running full width underneath them. Its replacement — the pane is the measure — reads well to about a thousand pixels and then sets 150-character lines on a wide stage. So there is one cap, expressed as the scroller's own inline padding (max(32px, (100% - 888px)/2)): every voice obeys it because nothing inside sets a width, and below ~950px it collapses to exactly the flat gutter it replaces.
donts: Don't build SaaS dashboard clichés: metric-card grids, gradient accents, or marketing gloss inside the product.

Don't drift toward the AI-chat startup look: sparkle icons, purple gradients, mascot energy, or a field of alternating bubbles. Amended by POD-993: the OPERATOR's turn in a transcript is a right-aligned card at a measure, because side is the cheapest possible statement of who spoke and it costs no colour, no label and no vertical space. The exception is one-sided and stays that way — the agent keeps the full column and the flat ground, and only the human's turn is a surface: the theme's one-step-off-the-sheet ground, a hairline rim, and a single lit pixel along its top edge, which is the same one resting elevation every other surface in this window is built from. The corner that points at the speaker is the one that is not round. Two columns of bubbles would halve the measure of the thing the reader actually came to read, which is the defect the original rule was aimed at.
Don't ship enterprise-DevOps-console sprawl: cluttered toolbars, inconsistent panels, Jenkins/Grafana utilitarianism.
Don't let it feel like Electron-app blandness — a website in a frame; the shell is an instrument with native manners.
Don't flat-fill an issue color, use terracotta or a signal hue as an issue color, or add a green anywhere in the Superade theme — its palette is neutral ink, yellow, red, blue.
Don't add perpetual motion that is not gated on the working mark's own predicate; stillness is the 'needs you' signal and must stay legible.
Don't use white text on Superade Yellow — ink on yellow is always Dark Ink; and don't put #f5c518 in a text token at all (gold writes on ink, ochre on paper).

Don't re-hue the neutrals. The dark chassis is neutral ink and the light one is warm stone; a tinted chrome competes with the issue-accent channel, whose whole premise is that a hue on a surface was chosen by somebody.
Don't add a second resting shadow. The stage sheet is the window's one elevation, and it only reads as one while nothing else at rest casts anything.
